name: shuar
confidence_why: Turner 1992 only names overlapping three-level accent and tone systems in Shuar and calls for more research, Kohlberger 2020 and Valeš 2017 say nothing about Shuar accent, and the descriptions that do analyse it (Turner 1958 as stress or tone and Gnerre 2010 as pitch accent, as Peña 2015 reports) could not be obtained, so the type and placement of Shuar word accent remain unknown here.

catalog_quote: Paralelo con las vocales orales indicadas, existen en los mismos puntos y formas de articulation juegos iguales que son nasalizados y susurrados. Ademas, parece que varios sistemas modificatorios se superponen principalmente a las vocales. Estos incluyen sistemas de acentuacion (tres niveles), entonacion (cuatro niveles), tonos (tres niveles), extension (dos tiempos) y ritmo. En la interaction de estos sistemas con las unidades sintacticas (los sintagmas, clausulas y oraciones), se manifiestan fenomenos de coyuntura entre las diferentes unidades. Hacen falta mas investigaciones, particularmente con instrumentos electronicos precisos, para poder llegar a conclusiones confiables en cuanto a los detalles de los sistemas. audit.reasoning: (1) Quote verified verbatim in the held Turner 1992 djvu text (lines 175-186, 1994, 2012, 2929-2935) and PDF pp. 2-3; only the printed page number is inferred. (2) The classification not determinable honestly reflects Turner 1992, a 1992 SIL grammar sketch that names a three-level accent system and explicitly defers analysis; but this is not the best available description. Kohlberger 2020's literature table (opened) and Valeš 2017 (opened) both show the Shuar phonology literature to be Turner 1958a/b, Turner 1992, Gnerre 1999/2010 and Saad 2014, with no dedicated accent study; Gnerre 2010 (172 pp, phonology chapter) and Saad 2014 (188 pp, phonology pp. 19-28) are unread and are the obvious candidates to contain an explicit accent statement. sources.citation: Kohlberger, Martin. 2020. A Grammatical Description of Shiwiar. Leiden University PhD; LOT Dissertation Series 573. Utrecht: LOT. 421 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: open copy online (also online with a university library login)
sources.quote: For SHIWIAR (sister language, not Shuar): 'every phonological word in Shiwiar only has one primary accent ... manifested phonetically by higher pitch, longer duration and increased amplitude' (p.137); 'Accent placement in Shiwiar is not predictable based on general phonotactic or metric principles. Even the claim that accent is lexically specified ... is hard to uphold because there is so much variation' (p.140); accent spreads rightward under vocative (tone-like). Table 2.2 lists Shuar sources as Gnerre 2010, Pellizaro 1969, Pellizaro & Náwech 2005, Saad 2014, Turner 1958a (phonology), 1958b,
sources.locator: sec. 5.3.3 'Accent', pp. 137-141; Table 2.2 'Literature on Chicham languages', pp. 18-19

sources.citation: Valeš, Miroslav. 2017. Influencia del español en el sistema vocálico shuar: vocales susurradas. Lexis 41(1): 203-230 (PUCP, open access).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.quote: No statement on accent/stress anywhere in the article (a full-text search for stress/accent/'tónic'/'tono' = 0 hits). p.206: 'la información disponible sobre la fonética y fonología shuar es insuficiente y bastante anticuada. Basándose en la descripción de Turner (1958a; 1992) y Gnerre (1999; 2010)...'; quotes Gnerre 2010 pp. 47-48, 64 on vowels (confirms Gnerre 2010 has a phonology chapter). Transcriptions mark an accent per word ([ipjáku], [ká:pɨ], dictionary form múukª) without comment.
sources.locator: p. 206-208 (sec. on Shuar vowel system); bibliography pp. 228-230
